messages.author: b431df4437cb4a5f
messages.subject: Error Running Blangiardo Camelleti Piemonte SPDE S-T Example
parts: I am trying to run some example SPDE spatial-temporal models in INLA and when running the Piemonte example from Blangiardo and Camelleti's book am getting the attached error. I am running INLA 22.7.1 in experimental mode and R4.2.2. Any idea what I might try to get around this or better yet, correct it?

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error Running Blangiardo Camelleti Piemonte SPDE S-T Example
parts:
Hi Daniel,

Looks like the memory limit has reached, even though you have enough memory in your system. I've tried this example in a laptop considering different setups on parallel computations (and memory use) and got CPU timings from 50 seconds up to 5-6 minutes, by decreasing the use of parallel computations (a lot is gain with changing to PARDISO library) and decreasing the memory use.

You can try lowering the use of memory by lowering the number of threads, such as
     inla(..., num.threads="4:1")
or down to
     inla(..., num.threads="1:1")

Best regards,
Elias

messages.author: a96aa45411c16ae6
messages.subject: Re: [External] Re: [r-inla] Error Running Blangiardo Camelleti Piemonte SPDE S-T Example
parts:
Dear all:

I am not sure it would help, but the code worked fine on my system (Ubuntu 20.04@WSL2 on Windows 11, num.threads="16:1", 112GB RAM, Intel Xeon W-2275). The model ran in 98 seconds without PARDISO, and the memory usage peaked at 11 GB (including the system use). I think that the GLIBC error in HPC systems can be solved by installing glibc 2.29 (but I guess the system administrator has the privilege to install new libraries on the HPC system).

Thank you.
Best,
Insang Song

Usually the CentOS7 one works well.
